title: wiretap: Add support for Chrome NetLog
description:
Adds support for reading Chrome's NetLog file format, as described at https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/network-stack/netlog/ .
Resolves https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20289 .

Agreed and thanks for taking care of it.
This (json_get_array_index) is NOT array accessed, it's list accessed.  I hope there is a better interface for iterating JSON objects.

I don't quite understand the wsjson API, but I think you should be doing something with json_get_next_object for this 1 for loop (so you don't have the nested for loops within json_get_array_index() each time the array index is incremented

I see that you're right - each iteration currently goes through all of the prior items, which is very inefficient. However, `json_get_next_object` is not exposed in wsjson.h. Would we want to add `json_get_next_object` to `wsjson.h` so we can call it directly?
@mmann78 : I've submitted https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20964 to expose `json_get_next_object`
And corresponding change made here!

It's frustrating that these are "dynamic" constants, so I'm not sure of the proper case for the member variables.  I originally thought the code in parse_json_events() should be a switch statement (with these constants), but quickly found out why it's a nested if/else.  Should these be lower case variable names?

Within the NetLog file, they are called "constants". While they aren't constant from a C perspective (because they can change between files), they are "constant" within the context of a single NetLog file. They are also capitalized because those are the exact names from within the NetLog file (as can be seen when they are retrieved in `parse_log_event_constants`).

IMHO, I think it may be worth keeping them as-is.
Based on the logic of the code, it looks like several JSON events are "mandatory".  Should missing elements be flagged instead of silently ignored (see !19800 for an example of what I mean)
What about "helper functions" for all of these types to make it easier to read a giant if/else block.
No objection. Do you want to do it or want me to do it?
You can do it as I think there are potentially bigger changes I definitely want you to do with other review comments.
@mmann78 : I've split off as much as I think I reasonably can into helper functions. Can you take a look?
It wasn't what I originally pictured, but there is much more common code there than I realized, so I do like the updated approach.
Did you check to see if something similar already exists?  I know IPv4:port is a popular string format, but I wasn't sure if IPv6:port was common enough that there's a string utility function for it.

I do like the functionality a lot, I just thought there were several performance/code improvements to be done. My changes were as follows:
1. Ran convert-glib-types.py (initially hoping it would fix my datatype conversion warnings - it did not)
2. Moved functions around so forward declarations aren't needed.  So diff from previous may be difficult, but going forward it should be easier.
3. Addressed John's comment (because I was in the area)
4. Addressed some whitespace issues (some tabs creeped into netlog.c)
5. g_malloc0 -> g_malloc when file data is immediately read afterwards.

I don't believe so, but you are assuming a perfectly formed file (which may not always be the case).
I think another big performance hit is the iteration over the JSON objects that you think are an array, but are actually a list.

Given that these are generated from Chrome/Edge, I think assuming it is valid Base64 is a reasonable assumption. And I don't think it's problematic because we'll do the actual base64 decoding (and validation) later when we emit the packet.

Do you have any concerns with using such a function here?
No, I think it's a worthwhile optimization.
Done

I only realized tonight that there's a `byte_count` field which I could read instead of calculating the base64 data. So I've removed that base64 processing code and am now using that field. That should be even more performent.
Is there any way we can turn this into a preference, so that it can be modified by end-users?
No, see #20234
